channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: China’s Plan to Make Yuan a Global Currency Enters Faster Phase
item.description: China’s campaign to promote the global use of the yuan appears to be accelerating as the authorities seek to build a more comprehensive financial ecosystem for the currency beyond just trade settlement.
item.dc:creator: Iris Ouyang

item.title: Hong Kong’s APEC Comeback Showcases a City Remade by Beijing
item.description: Hong Kong lost the chance to host a key gathering of global finance ministers 12 years ago as pro-democracy protests loomed. Now, Beijing is giving it another chance in a city where its tightening grip has made such dissent all but unthinkable.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan and Kiuyan Wong

item.title: Asian Stocks Set for Gains as Tech Selloff Eases: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian equities were primed to rebound Friday after dip buyers powered a recovery on Wall Street from a chip-stock selloff fueled by concerns about the artificial intelligence trade. Treasuries rallied on haven demand and the dollar slipped.
item.dc:creator: Toby Alder

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 16
item.description: Oil was set for a second weekly advance as increasing Middle East supply risks weighed against a fresh release of emergency reserves.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: The Investment Lessons Learned from 1873
item.description: Long before the Great Depression or the 2008 financial crisis, the world endured its first truly global financial crash. In his new book, 1873: The Rothschilds, the First Great Depression, and the Making of the Modern World, Pulitzer Prize–winning author Liaquat Ahamed traces how a booming global bond market, railroad speculation and massive flows of capital helped fuel extraordinary growth before the bubble burst. At the center of the story were the Rothschilds, the powerful banking dynasty that helped transform government borrowing and global finance. Ahamed joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss why 1873 still matters, how railroad mania compares with today’s rush into AI infrastructure, and what the era can teach investors about bubbles, monetary-policy mistakes and financial resilience. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hot US Inflation, Treasury Safe Haven, CoreWeave's Credit Risk
item.description: "Bloomberg Real Yield" highlights the market-moving news you need to know. Today's guests: Societe Generale Americas Head of Research Subadra Rajappa, Columbia Threadneedle Investments Global Head, Fixed Income Gene Tannuzzo, BoFA Securities head of US Credit Strategy Neha Khoda, and JPMorgan Asset Management Fixed Income Portfolio Manager Stephanie Doyle. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Porsche CEO With a First Look at Mission S Sports Car
item.description: At a world premiere in Queens, Porsche CEO Michael Leiters told Bloomberg’s Matt Miller that the company’s new sports car will launch a distinct model line positioned well above the 911. The mid-engine platform is designed to support several variants and is flexible enough for either hybrid or combustion-only powertrains. The two speak on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ross Gerber on Tesla Roadster, Potential SpaceX Merger
item.description: Ross Gerber discussed Tesla’s anticipated Roadster unveiling, following a Barclays note suggesting Tesla and SpaceX could merge before year-end, potentially ahead of Tesla’s annual general meeting. Gerber said a high-priced car made in low volumes would not materially affect Tesla financially. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Porsche CEO Leiters on New Luxury Supercar, China and EVs
item.description: Porsche AG unveiled a concept previewing a new supercar, the Mission S, that will be positioned above the 911 in its lineup. Speaking with Matt Miller on "Bloomberg The Close," Porsche CEO Michael Leiters discusses the new supercar and also comments on the state of the China market, the future of electric vehicles and the German automaker's storied legacy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: MSCI Weighs Indonesia Downgrade, Removal From Global Indexes
item.description: Indonesia faces a potential ejection from global stock indexes after MSCI Inc. said the country no longer merits emerging-market status, escalating the threat of foreign investor flight as concerns deepen over market integrity.
item.dc:creator: Jackie Edwards and Prima Wirayani

item.title: Big Take: What Is the US Economy Trying to Tell Us?
item.description: On today’s Big Take podcast, editors Matt Boesler and Cristina Lindblad join Sarah Holder to unpack what the data says is happening in the US economy and why consumer sentiment tells another story. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inflation Pointing for the Fed to Act: Rajappa
item.description: Gene Tannuzzo, global head of fixed income at Columbia Threadneedle Investments, and Subadra Rajappa, head of research at Société Générale Americas, join Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." US producer prices rose in September at the fastest pace in more than four years as higher energy costs reverberated through the US economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rate Volatility Might Shake Fundamentals: Tannuzzo
item.description: Gene Tannuzzo, global head of fixed income at Columbia Threadneedle Investments, and Subadra Rajappa, head of research at Société Générale Americas, join Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Treasuries led a global bond rally as a selloff in artificial-intelligence shares deepened, spurring demand for havens from a growth slowdown. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Senate Race Will Come Down to Turnout, Says Siena's Levy
item.description: Don Levy, director of the Siena Research Institute, said that while the Democratic party itself is not gaining in popularity, 'change' is what's on top of mind for voters, and 'they want their lives to be better' and see voting as a way to do that. Levy also discussed the fight for Latino voters in Texas and other sunbelt states and said that many voters believe that ICE tactics go too far. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Indexing Sports: How Team Stats Become Tradeable Assets
item.description: In this episode, we explore the financial infrastructure behind the new crop of sports ETF filings and indexes that measure the performance of individual teams.
item.dc:creator: Eric Balchunas and Joel Weber

item.title: Harvard Fund Hits Record $68 Billion After 27% Annual Return
item.description: Harvard University’s endowment jumped to a record $68 billion as successful bets on equities and venture capital including SpaceX holdings helped the richest US college weather an unprecedented pressure campaign from President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Janet Lorin

item.title: Muni Bond Rally Sends Yields Down the Most Since April 2025
item.description: State and local debt prices rallied across the curve on Thursday, with 10-year municipal bonds surging the most since last April, in line with a similar move in the US Treasury market.
item.dc:creator: Aashna Shah

item.title: IEA Agrees to Release of Outstanding 100 Million Oil Barrels
item.description: The International Energy Agency said that member countries agreed to complete the release of 100 million barrels of oil that are still outstanding from an intervention in March aimed at cooling high fuel prices.
item.dc:creator: Grant Smith and Ewa Krukowska

item.title: Chocolate Demand Roars Back as Cocoa Grindings Beat Forecast
item.description: Cocoa processing in Europe and Asia exceeded expectations by wide margins in the third quarter, signaling a potentially stronger-than-anticipated recovery in global demand after years of elevated chocolate prices.
item.dc:creator: Anuradha Raghu, Cole Martin and Will Standring

item.title: Gold Rallies as Lower Yields, AI Stock Selloff Fuel Haven Demand
item.description: Gold increased as an equity selloff drove investors into bonds, pushing Treasury yields lower.
item.dc:creator: Mariana Durao and Yihui Xie
